verses.author: model_A
verses.text: The market empties out and the pigeons take the square.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Grey wings settle on the news no one came to read—
one bird pecks at yesterday's headline
folded wet against the curb.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A crust falls where the print bleeds through—
he chooses that over truth,
and flies with what he can carry.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Nothing left in his mouth but the taste of ink—
still he sings from the wire
like it was the whole story.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Dusk rusts along the wire, and the song thins out—
somewhere a shutter comes down
on the last stall selling bread.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The vendor counts coins that won't add up tonight—
he pockets the loss like a stone,
walks home under wires gone quiet.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
His shadow trails long past the shuttered stalls—
somewhere a door creaks open,
a lamp still burns for no one.
motifs: a lamp burning for no one

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The lamp gutters low, waiting on nobody's return—
moths keep the vigil instead,
tapping the glass like small debts.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Morning finds the wick drowned in its own wax—
someone sweeps the moths from the sill,
counts them like coins that finally add up.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The broom pauses at the threshold, unsure of its work—
dust settles where the debts once flew,
the sill remembers what the hand forgets.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A crack in the wood holds the last of the light—
someone's fingerprint, someone's rain,
the sill keeping ledger of hands long gone.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The rain finds the same crack, patient as an old debt—
it asks nothing of the fingerprint,
just fills what's already hollow.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The hollow learns the shape of enough—
water sits still where it's welcomed,
no longer asking the wood to be whole.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
A sparrow drinks from the wood's small cup—
what was broken now holds a whole sky,
enough for one bird's thirst.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The sky in the cup ripples, then settles—
the sparrow gone, its thirst folded into flight,
the wood keeping what little heaven it borrowed.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Borrowed heaven leaves no debt behind—
the wood darkens, dries, forgets the shape of sky,
content again to just be wood.
